
Three arXiv papers from the RSS scout meet ≥3 inclusion criteria with strong harness-layer relevance: SDOF addresses state-constrained tool dispatch in multi-agent orchestration, Verifiable Agentic Infrastructure proposes proof-derived authorization at the harness layer, and SkillSmith compiles agent skills into boundary-guided runtime interfaces.

## Suggestions

- [SDOF: Taming the Alignment Tax in Multi-Agent Orchestration with State-Constrained Dispatch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15204) — Proposes a state-constrained dispatch framework for multi-agent orchestration that reduces the alignment tax — empirical evidence that harness-layer dispatch design directly affects agent reliability and safety.
  Section: Research Papers > Tool & API Integration Layers | Criteria: Manages tool dispatch, context handling, state management, or safety constraints at the harness layer, Evaluates or benchmarks agent behavior through controlled harness-mediated interactions, Empirical or production evidence of harness design improving reliability, safety, or performance

- [Verifiable Agentic Infrastructure: Proof-Derived Authorization for Sovereign AI Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15228) — Introduces a harness-layer authorization framework using cryptographic proofs to gate agent actions, providing verifiable safety constraints at the execution infrastructure level.
  Section: Research Papers > Safety & Constraint Infrastructure | Criteria: Defines or implements the execution loop, scaffolding, or runtime environment that hosts an AI agent, Manages tool dispatch, context handling, state management, or safety constraints at the harness layer, Empirical or production evidence of harness design improving reliability, safety, or performance

- [SkillSmith: Compiling Agent Skills into Boundary-Guided Runtime Interfaces](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15215) — Compiles agent skills into constrained runtime interfaces with explicit action boundaries — a scaffolding-layer approach to constraining agent behavior at the harness level.
  Section: Research Papers > Agent-Computer Interfaces & Scaffolding Design | Criteria: Defines or implements the execution loop, scaffolding, or runtime environment that hosts an AI agent, Manages tool dispatch, context handling, state management, or safety constraints at the harness layer, Evaluates or benchmarks agent behavior through controlled harness-mediated interactions
